record.context_brief: Rigorous proof of fast WSK mixing
record.original_question: For the full WSK algorithm in the q=3 Potts antiferromagnet on n x n periodic square lattices at and down to zero temperature, can one rigorously prove rapid mixing behavior consistent with the numerically observed constant-time mixing (absence of critical slowing down)?

evidence.quote: For the full WSK algorithm, numerical data strongly suggest that there is constant-time mixing ... for the q = 3 model on n x n periodic square lattices ... It would be wonderful to be able to prove something!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the q=3 Potts antiferromagnet on the n×n square lattice with periodic boundary conditions. The state space is the set of configurations σ:V→{1,2,3} where V is the vertex set of the torus, and the Hamiltonian is H(σ)=∑_{{x,y}∈E} δ_{σ(x),σ(y)} (E being the edge set). For inverse temperature β∈[0,∞], the Gibbs measure is μ_β(σ)∝exp(−βH(σ)), interpreted at β=∞ as the uniform measure on proper 3-colorings of the torus.

The Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký (WSK) algorithm is the following Markov chain on configurations: at each step, choose uniformly at random an unordered pair {a,b}⊂{1,2,3}, consider the subgraph induced by vertices σ^{-1}({a,b}), identify its connected components (clusters), and independently for each cluster either swap the colors a↔b on it or leave it unchanged, with probabilities determined by the standard WSK rule that leaves μ_β reversible (at β=∞, each cluster is flipped independently with probability 1/2).

Let τ_mix(n,β) denote the total-variation mixing time of this chain on the n×n torus at inverse temperature β.

Prove rigorously that, for the family of n for which the chain is ergodic, τ_mix(n,β) remains bounded by a constant (or grows at most polylogarithmically) uniformly in n as n→∞, for all β∈[0,∞], thereby establishing the absence of critical slowing down observed numerically.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2022 study on ergodicity of the WSK algorithm) has clarified ergodicity questions—WSK is ergodic on bipartite graphs for q≥2 but non-ergodic at zero temperature for q=3 on 3m×3n tori with gcd(m,n)=1—yet a rigorous proof of rapid (constant-time) mixing matching the numerical observations on n×n periodic square lattices has not been found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ergodicity of the Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký algorithm on bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Ergodicity established for WSK on bipartite graphs; non-ergodicity for q=3 at zero temperature on 3m×3n square lattices with gcd(m,n)=1.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity is settled in some cases but quantitative rapid mixing is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: A Personal List of Unsolved Problems Concerning Lattice Gases and Antiferromagnetic Potts Models
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an unsolved problem concerning antiferromagnetic Potts models.
status_evidence.claim: Rapid mixing of WSK for q=3 Potts AF on the square lattice appears as an open problem.
